question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int 3\sin\left(3 - 7 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}} $+C$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=3 - 7 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-7,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(- \frac{1}{7}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 3\sin\left(3 - 7 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=3\left(- \frac{1}{7}\right)\int \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{3}{7}\int \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{3}{7}\left(-\cos\left(u\right)\right)+C\\ &=\frac{3}{7}\cos\left(3 - 7 x\right)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{10}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{5}} 6\cos\left(5 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=5 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=5,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{3 \pi}{10}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=5\left(\frac{3 \pi}{10}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{3 \pi}{2}\\ x=\frac{2 \pi}{5}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=5\left(\frac{2 \pi}{5}\right)+\left(0\right)=2 \pi.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{10}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{5}} 6\cos\left(5 x\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=6\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{2 \pi} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{6}{5}\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{2 \pi} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{6}{5}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{2 \pi}\\ &=\frac{6}{5}\left(\sin\left(2 \pi\right)-\sin\left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{6}{5}\left(\left(0\right)-\left(-1\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{6}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{\pi}{36}}^{\frac{\pi}{36}} 8\cos\left(6 x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=6 x + \frac{\pi}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=6,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\pi}{36}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=6\left(- \frac{\pi}{36}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}\\ x=\frac{\pi}{36}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=6\left(\frac{\pi}{36}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{- \frac{\pi}{36}}^{\frac{\pi}{36}} 8\cos\left(6 x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=8\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\left(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\left(\left(1\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{\frac{4 \pi}{9}}^{\frac{8 \pi}{9}} 8\sin\left(\frac{3 x}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\frac{3 x}{4}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{3}{4},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{4 \pi}{9}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{4 \pi}{9}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}\\ x=\frac{8 \pi}{9}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{8 \pi}{9}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{2 \pi}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{4 \pi}{9}}^{\frac{8 \pi}{9}} 8\sin\left(\frac{3 x}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=8\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{3}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{32}{3}\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{3}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{32}{3}\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{3}}\\ &=- \frac{32}{3}\left(\cos\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)-\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{32}{3}\left(\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{32}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{15 \pi}{4}}^{\frac{5 \pi}{24}} \frac{4}{3}\sin\left(- \frac{2 x}{5} + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=- \frac{2 x}{5} + \frac{\pi}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=- \frac{2}{5},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(- \frac{5}{2}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{15 \pi}{4}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=- \frac{2}{5}\left(- \frac{15 \pi}{4}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{11 \pi}{6}\\ x=\frac{5 \pi}{24}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=- \frac{2}{5}\left(\frac{5 \pi}{24}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

The transformed bounds decrease because the inner derivative is negative. Keep their order together with the negative substitution factor.

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{- \frac{15 \pi}{4}}^{\frac{5 \pi}{24}} \frac{4}{3}\sin\left(- \frac{2 x}{5} + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=\frac{4}{3}\left(- \frac{5}{2}\right)\int_{\frac{11 \pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{10}{3}\int_{\frac{11 \pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{10}{3}\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{11 \pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\\ &=\frac{10}{3}\left(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-\cos\left(\frac{11 \pi}{6}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{10}{3}\left(\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{5 \sqrt{3}}{3} + \frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{4 \pi}{9}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{5}{2}\cos\left(\frac{3 x}{2} + \pi\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\frac{3 x}{2} + \pi.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{3}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{4 \pi}{9}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{3}{2}\left(- \frac{4 \pi}{9}\right)+\left(\pi\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}\\ x=\frac{\pi}{2}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)+\left(\pi\right)=\frac{7 \pi}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{- \frac{4 \pi}{9}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{5}{2}\cos\left(\frac{3 x}{2} + \pi\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=\frac{5}{2}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{7 \pi}{4}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{5}{3}\int_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{7 \pi}{4}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{5}{3}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{7 \pi}{4}}\\ &=\frac{5}{3}\left(\sin\left(\frac{7 \pi}{4}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{5}{3}\left(\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{5 \sqrt{3}}{6} - \frac{5 \sqrt{2}}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
